analysis.message: This patient exhibits a classic reactive hypoglycemia pattern. Despite excellent overall glycemic control, the consistent post-lunch drops below 70 mg/dL suggest an overproduction of insulin lagging behind the glucose absorption from earlier meals. A small, complex-carbohydrate snack mid-morning may stabilize this trend.

analysis.message: This T2 patient has excellent baseline glucose control but exhibits a clear dietary pattern: high-fat lunches cause delayed nocturnal hyperglycemia 8-10 hours later. The daytime metabolism handles the initial glucose load well, but the prolonged fat absorption overwhelms nighttime insulin sensitivity.

patterns.name: Delayed Evening Hyperglycemia with High-Fat Meals

analysis.message: This patient struggles with a dual burden: a dawn phenomenon causing elevated fasting glucose, which is then compounded by delayed nocturnal hyperglycemia from high-fat lunches. This combination results in a near-24-hour hyperglycemic profile on high-fat days. Both overnight medication adjustments and dietary fat restriction are necessary.

analysis.message: This T1 patient demonstrates a clear and severe delayed hyperglycemic response to dietary fat. The standard lunch bolus adequately covers the initial glucose rise but fails to address the prolonged absorption phase 8-10 hours later. Implementing extended dual-wave boluses for high-fat meals is strongly recommended.

patterns.name: Delayed Nocturnal Hyperglycemia with High-Fat Meals

analysis.message: Despite elevated morning readings, this patient consistently experiences post-lunch reactive hypoglycemia. The pattern suggests excessive endogenous insulin secretion in response to small carbohydrate loads. Adjusting meal composition to include more complex carbohydrates and fiber at lunch may prevent the rapid drop.
